title: USE OF PLANT FIBERS TO IMPROVE FLAVOR OF FERMENTED PRODUCTS
abstract: The present disclosure relates generally to the use of plant fibers or starches to enhance the taste or texture of fermented dairy and dairy analogue products. In some embodiments, the dairy analogue products are vegan yogurt products formed from the fermentation of plant milks, such as soy milk, almond milk, hazelnut milk, sesame milk, pistachio milk, potato milk, banana milk, flaxseed milk, macadamia nut milk, cashew milk, oat milk, hemp milk, coconut milk, and pea-derived milks. In some embodiments, the plant fibers include pectin, inulin, fruit fiber (such as apple fiber or citrus fiber), starch, oat fiber, pea fiber, seaweed fiber, and any combinations thereof. In some embodiments, the enhancement of taste or texture includes reducing a green vegetal taste, reducing a sour taste, increasing a sweet taste, reducing a bitter taste, reducing an astringent taste, increasing firmness, reducing a grainy texture, increasing thickness, increasing mouthfeel, or any combination thereof. In certain related aspects, the disclosure provides comestible compositions that include fermented plant milk and a plant fiber or starch.

abstract: The present invention relates to a method for the preparation of a carob powder, in particular a carob powder with a low content of butanoic acid, which can be used as base ingredient characterized by a color, sensory profile, and volatile compounds similar to cocoa powder. title: A MEAT CULTURE CONSTRUCT FOR A MEAT CULTURE BIOREACTOR MODULE
abstract: A meat culture construct for a meat culture bioreactor module (102) that is attachable to a meat culturing system (100). The meat culture bioreactor module (102) has a housing (108) adapted to receive the meat culture construct for culturing cells on the meat culture construct within the housing. The meat culture construct comprises a plurality of fibres (120) and an end support (126). The plurality of fibres (120) have external surfaces for cell adhesion and culturing, and ends embedded within the end support (126) and extending from the end support (126) such they extend into the housing (108) when the meat culture construct is received in the housing of the meat culture bioreactor module (102). At a plane coincident with the end support (126) the plurality of fibres (120) are arranged in a fibre distribution defining an envelope. The fibre distribution comprises a Fibre Distribution Parameter, FDP, of between 9 cm3 and 24 cm3, the FDP being the product of the sum of the circumferences of the plurality of fibres within the envelope and the area within the envelope not occupied by the plurality of fibres.

title: METHOD FOR PRODUCING A MILK SUBSTITUTE PRODUCT
abstract: The invention relates to a method for producing a milk substitute, comprising, in a first method step, providing a dry ingredient mixture comprising at least one main vegetable ingredient, wherein the main vegetable ingredient is dry-milled oat flour and the milk substitute to be produced is oat milk, a first enzyme, a second enzyme, and a co-factor for heat-stabilizing one of the enzymes. The heat-stabilizing co-factor is in the form of CaCl<sub>2</sub>, and the weight ratio of the co-factor to the one enzyme that is heat-stabilized by the co-factor is between 1:1 and 2.5:1, preferably between 1.66:1 and 2:1. Furthermore, the weight ratio of the oat flour to water is between 1:4 and 1:10, preferably between 1:7 and 1:9. The first enzyme is in the form of heat-stable endo-alpha-amylase. Furthermore, the amount of the first enzyme, based on the dry oat content, is between 0.2 and 0.6 percent by weight, preferably 0.4 percent by weight. Furthermore, the second enzyme is designed as a heat-unstable maltogenic alpha-amylase. The amount of the second enzyme, based on the dry oat content, is between 0.15 and 0.45 percent by weight, preferably 0.3 percent by weight. In a second process step, water with a maximum temperature of 60 °C is provided; in a third process step, the dry ingredient mixture is added to the water while stirring to obtain a suspension; and in a fourth process step, the finished milk substitute product is removed within a period of 40 to 60 minutes after the dry ingredient mixture has been added. Advantageously, the process is energy-saving, as only a relatively low temperature is required, and furthermore, the process duration is short due to the relatively short time of 40 to 60 minutes until the finished milk substitute product is removed.

title: Method and bioreactor system for producing mycelium biomass
abstract: A method for producing mycelium biomass. The method comprises obtaining a base media composition and an antifoam solution; sterilizing a mixture of the base media composition and the antifoam solution under a first set of parameters such as for sterilisation; adding an autoclaved organic carbon source solution to the mixture, controlling a second set of parameters such as may be for growth and adding an inoculum culture medium and mixing the inoculum culture medium in the mixture to form a first composition. During the growth phase the first composition is subject to a variable aeration rate programme. The mycelium biomass is harvested and may be prepared as a food product. Also disclosed is a bioreactor system for producing mycelium biomass.

title: Biomass, methods and bioreactor systems
abstract: A large fungal mycelium biomass of densely packed non-dispersed hyphal structures is cultured in an aerated, agitated liquid culture system in order to produce a compactable or mouldable product suitable for use and presentation as a food product intended to resemble a whole cut of meat with the hyphae replicating muscle strand structure. The biomass may be distinguished by its cohesive integral structure and is preferably derived from a fungal species such as Rhizopus oligosporus, Rhizopus microspores, Rhizopus oryzae Aspergillus niger, Neurospora spp. or Fusarium venenatum. The biomass may reach 3-50 cm in diameter. A method of aerated culture from a spore inoculation at 20-40 C, pH4-8, with agitation preferably at 50-600rpm is disclosed. A method of moulding the cultured biomass in a perforated mould to remove excess moisture and shape the product is disclosed, preferably the product is further flavoured, sliced. The use of various fungal species in a food product and the use of a mould to shape a mycelium biomass are disclosed. A bioreactor system comprising a vessel with aeration unit is disclosed.

title: METHOD FOR PRODUCING A DISSOLVABLE COFFEE BODY, AND COFFEE BODY
abstract: In a method for producing a dissolvable coffee body, liquid coffee extract is poured into a recess of a cast mould and the coffee extract poured into the recess is frozen and then freeze-dried, thereby producing the dissolvable coffee body. In a first time period of freeze-drying, a freeze-drying device is operated at a first temperature in the positive °Celsius range and at least one first pressure of greater than 0.4 mbar. In a second time period of freeze-drying, after the first time period, the freeze-drying device is operated at at least one second temperature in the positive °Celsius range and at least one second pressure, the at least one second pressure being lower than the first pressure. The method uses relatively high temperatures in freeze-drying and only a low negative pressure compared to atmospheric pressure. This reduces the time needed for freeze-drying and a mechanically stable coffee body or coffee cube having good dissolving properties is obtained.

title: Equipment and method for roasting food
abstract: The invention relates to an apparatus for automatically roasting food. The apparatus comprises a housing (1) adapted for placement over a driven conveyor belt movable in a conveying direction (3), on which, in use, the food (2) to be roasted is placed, and an electric hot air generator (4) provided in the housing and connected to the housing, wherein, in use, the electric hot air generator is located above the conveyor belt. The electric hot air generator comprises a heating element and a blower nozzle (5). In use, the air heated by the heating element is blown out through the blower nozzle as the conveyor belt moves, in an outflow direction towards the food on the conveyor belt at an angle relative to the conveying direction, the angle having a value in the range of 30° to 85°.

title: MICROPARTICLES CONTAINING ALGAL PROTEINS AND USES THEREOF
abstract: The present disclosure relates generally to microparticles containing algal proteins and their use in various applications. In some embodiments, the microparticles are precipitates. In some other embodiments, the microparticles are coacervates. In some embodiments, the microparticles are core-shell microcapsules having a hydrophobic core material encapsulated by a shell that contains an algal protein. In some embodiments, the hydrophobic core material comprises a flavor oil, a fragrance oil, or a combination thereof. In certain aspects, the disclosure provides the use of such microparticles to improve the texture, mouthfeel, perceived fattiness, or perceived creaminess of a comestible article. In some embodiments, the comestible article is a vegan dairy product, a vegan meat product, or a vegan seafood product. In certain aspects, the disclosure provides the use of the microparticles to provide a fragrance to a fragranced product, such as a personal care product, a laundry product, or a cosmetic product.

title: METHOD FOR PRODUCING A TEXTURATE AND PROTEIN-CONTAINING TEXTURATE
abstract: The invention relates to a protein-containing texturate which is characterised by a special anisotropy comparable to meat. The texturate comprises a first protein mixture with a non-legume protein, in particular wheat protein, with a proportion of between 10 wt.% and 90 wt.% of the dry mass, and a second protein mixture, in particular with a legume protein or a side-stream product, with a proportion of between 10 wt.% and 90 wt.% of the dry mass. The moisture content is less than 40 wt.% and in particular less than 35 wt.%; a protein proportion of the texturate is between 35 wt.% and 60 wt.% of the dry mass. According to the invention, the texturate has fibres with a preferred direction and a length of more than 10 mm and in particular more than 15 mm, and has an anisotropy index of greater than 1 and in particular greater than 1.4.

title: METHOD FOR PRODUCING A TEXTURATE AND EXTRUDER ASSEMBLY
abstract: The invention relates to a method for producing a texturate, in which a protein mixture is provided, comprising at least one first protein mixture, in particular a pea protein mixture or a broad bean protein mixture, with a weight proportion of between 45 wt.% and 75 wt.% relative to a base mixture. Water is added in a weight proportion of between 25 wt.% and 50 wt.% in relation to the basic mixture to form a dough and the dough is then extruded at a maximum temperature of between 110°C and 160°C to form an extrudate. The extrudate undergoes an elongation deformation at a temperature of greater than 100 °C by feeding the extrudate through an elongation nozzle, wherein the geometry thereof changes over its length such that a longitudinal and/or transverse elongation strain is generated on the mass.

title: Nutritional composition and method for optimizing protein quality in a product containing a vegetable protein source
abstract: A method of manufacturing a composition having an optimal protein mass includes determining a ratio of a first protein source to a second protein source having an optimal protein mass using an optimal model, and manufacturing a composition having protein sources of the ratio. abstract: The present invention relates to a method for analysis of a sample for the presence and/or quantity of cellular and/or viral target nucleic acids by means of hybridization between a hybridization agent and the target nucleic acids, the method comprises rendering cells or viruses in the sample permeable to hybridization agent including adding one or more enzymes to the sample to enzymatically degrade the sample and/or to contribute to rendering the cells or virus permeable to hybridization agent; adding one or more hybridization agents to said sample; facilitating hybridization between the one or more hybridization agents and the target nucleic acids to form hybridized target nucleic acids; and detecting, qualitatively or quantitatively, the hybridized target nucleic acids; wherein the one or more hybridization agents and the one or more enzymes are added to the sample so as to provide a mixture comprising the sample, the added one or more enzymes and the added one or more added hybridization agents, in which mixture the hybridization is facilitated.

abstract: The invention relates to the field of plant protein-based foods. abstract: In an iron (II) citrate monohydrate, identified by the formula FeC6H6O7-H2O ( Ferrous citrate monohydrate or iron citrate (II) monohydrate), obtained according to a particular production method, citric acid and elemental iron are bound in a molecular complex where the iron is agglomerated in the citrate which moves to a cyclic form and the iron is bound to the O groups of the carboxylic groups 1 and 3 through ionic bonds, forming two enantiomers, D and L (R and S), both perfectly water-soluble and highly assimilable by the human body. Formula (L) & Formula (D). title: Beverage product
abstract: A product for preparing a beverage comprising a fibre containing ingredient coated with beverage ingredient powder(s) and a sugar. title: Food supplement
abstract: A container contains a liquid food supplement and can be placed in a domestic freezer to provide a frozen food supplement. The liquid supplement may comprise, per 100 ml, 2-10g protein, 5-15g starch, and 20-50g water, and may further include 1-5g fibre, up to 8g fat and/or up to 3g vitamins and minerals. The total carbohydrate content of the liquid food supplement may be 25-45g per 100 ml, and the energy content may be 50-300 kcal per 100g. The protein may be derived from a non-animal source, e.g. pea protein, and the supplement may be dairy-free and/or vegan. The starch may be tapioca starch. Use of the container and a method of providing a frozen food supplement by placing the container in a freezer are also claimed. The liquid food supplement, the food supplement when chilled, and the food supplement when frozen are also claimed. The frozen food supplement may comprise a dispersion of ice crystals distributed in a freeze-concentrated liquid phase. The frozen food supplement may be in the form of a sorbet, iced smoothie or ice lolly. The liquid, chilled or frozen food supplement for use in maintaining or increasing body weight is also claimed.

title: Method for modifying the texture of foodstuff via alpha-glucan, preferably produced in situ
abstract: Disclosed herein are methods of producing a food product or food precursor. The methods may include (a) providing a food product/precursor comprising at least water and sucrose, and (b) contacting the food product/precursor with at least one Glucosyltransferase (GTF) and, in some aspects, a second enzyme that utilizes sucrose as a substrate, such as an invertase. The one or more GTFs may be selected from (i) a GTF that synthesizes α -1, 6-glucan, and/or (ii) a GTF that synthesizes α -1, 3-glucan. Such enzymatic treatments typically result in the production of alpha-glucan in the food product/precursor. Treatment of a food product/precursor with a second enzyme that utilizes sucrose as a substrate may alter the effect of GTF treatment on the food product/precursor, such as texture formation, sugar composition, and/or sweetness. Food products and food precursors produced by such methods are also disclosed.

abstract: The present document relates to a protein structuring module for a providing arrangement for manufacturing of a food product, using a protein constituent. The module establishes a shear stress for aligning molecules of the protein constituent, by including a first and a second solid part. The first solid parts are detachably connected to each other along their contact surfaces, and at least one of said contact surfaces includes a groove running across the surface. Together, as connected, the groove in the contact surfaces of the connected first and second solid parts define a shear channel of the cell having a first open end and a second open end. The open ends define an inlet and an outlet for conveying the structured protein substance.

title: Liquid distribution manifold
abstract: A liquid distribution manifold for an automated beverage preparation system. The manifold has a channel 120 with at least one branch 130. The channel 120 has an integral seal 150, aligned with the branch opening. The integral seal can be open (Fig. 2E), so the branch 130 is in fluid communication with the main channel 120; or the integral seal can be pinched closed (Fig. 2F), so that the branch 130 is closed. When the branch is sealed, liquid can still flow around the seal through the main channel 120, e.g., via flow paths 122. The manifold may have multiple branches and corresponding integral seals, and may be formed of an elastomeric material such as silicone. This manifold minimises dead-legs, in which stagnant liquid could be retained, and facilitates cleaning by flushing, thus aiding hygiene.

title: Apparatus for cleaning a liquid uptake conduit
abstract: An apparatus 1 for cleaning a liquid uptake conduit comprises a first conduit 3 for the flow of a first liquid in a first flow path. The first conduit 3 has an inlet and an outlet. A shroud element 4 is deployable between a first configuration and a second configuration. In the first configuration, the shroud element 4 is arranged to enclose a first portion 5 of the first conduit 3, such that a second portion of the first conduit 3 is uncovered by the shroud element 4 and corresponds with a storage volume for receiving a container 2. The inlet of the first conduit 3 is configured for the uptake of the first liquid from the container 2. In the second configuration, the shroud element 4 is arranged to enclose the first 5 and second portions of the first conduit 3, to provide a second flow path for the flow of a second liquid between an outer surface of the first conduit 3 and an inner surface of the shroud element 4, from the outlet towards the inlet of the first conduit 3.

title: Method for producing instant vegetable steaks based on beetroot flesh and a steak produced using this method
abstract: The subject of the application is an instant vegetable steak containing a mixture of at least one type of flour, dried vegetables, spices and roasted buckwheat flakes, textured pea protein, mushroom and roasted linseed, in which a functional additive made of beetroot pulp is added to the steak ingredients in the amount of 4 - 9% by weight in the form of crushed cubes or powder, and the amount of the remaining ingredients is in the range of 14 to 15% by weight of dried roasted buckwheat flakes, 15 to 16% by weight of dried textured pea protein, 15 to 16% by weight of pumpkin flour, 17 to 19% by weight of chickpea flour, dried onion 2% by weight, dried garlic 2% by weight, dried parsley 2% by weight, dried black pepper 0.2% by weight, dried lovage leaves 2% by weight dried cumin seeds 0.5% by weight, dried smoked paprika 3% by weight, dried boletus mushroom 8% by weight, roasted linseed 10% by weight and Himalayan salt 0.3% by weight. The application also covers a method for producing instant vegetable steak based on beet pulp, characterized in that in the first stage, fresh storage root (tuber) of beetroot is subjected to the process of washing, cleaning and peeling and it is crushed so that it is preferably shaped into cubes, preferably with dimensions not smaller than 2.0 x 2.0 cm, which are subjected to the process of freezing at a temperature of (-18°C) - (-30°C) for a period of 12 hours, then it is subjected to the process of osmotic dehydration and the obtained crushed pulp is immersed in an aqueous solution containing inulin and iron (II) sulfate 7-hydrate in a weight ratio of 6:1 (e.g. 300 g of solution + 50 g of beet pulp), placed in tightly closed, preferably glass vessels, in a heated water bath and shaken, and then the solution is removed from the beet pulp, which is then filtered on a filter with a weight of 87 [g/m<sup>2</sup>] and then frozen to a temperature of (-18°C) - (-30°C) for 24 hours, the dehydrated and frozen beet pulp is dried in a freeze-dryer, preferably at a temperature of +20°C on the heating shelf, maintaining a vacuum of 1,030 mBar and a maximum pressure of 1,600 mBar) for 22 hours, the drying process of the beet particles is carried out until the water content is in the range of 6 - 8%, after drying the beet pulp is ground in a cryogenic mill, during which the plant preparation is pre-frozen for about 10 minutes and kept at a low temperature, preferably at a temperature of (-194°C) throughout the entire grinding cycle (2-3 min) using a magnetic grinder and vibration frequency preferably 20 - 30 HZ, after which the obtained dried beetroot is mixed with dried vegetables, pumpkin flour, chickpea flour, roasted buckwheat flakes, textured pea protein, boletus mushroom and Himalayan salt, and the obtained mixture is preferably divided into portions of 150 g.

title: ADVANCED NITRITE REPLACEMENT IN PROCESSED MEATS, FISH, AND DAIRY: MULTIFUNCTIONAL FOOD INGREDIENTS FOR ENHANCED PRESERVATION AND HEALTH BENEFITS
abstract: The present invention introduces innovative Multifunctional Food Ingredients (MFIs) designed to replace sodium nitrite in processed meats, fish and dairy. These MFIs are formulated from plant-based extracts of polyphenols, known for their antioxidant, and antipathogenic properties, efficacy in food preservation, colour stabilisation, and a broad spectrum of health advantages, further enhanced by dietary fibre. This invention directly addresses public health concerns linked to the consumption of nitrite food additives and their associated risks of colon cancer and cardiovascular diseases. Furthermore, the synergistic combination of polyphenols and dietary fibres provides enhanced benefits for gut health, marking a significant advancement in the formulation of food additives. Additionally, this invention aligns with the global shift towards sustainable, eco-friendly bioproducts, contributing to the reduction of agri-food waste.

abstract: ABSTRACT: Die for the extrusion of a material rich in protein and water, as well as a system for the continuous preparation of an extruded food product, comprising such a die. This die (200) comprises a tubular casing (210), centred on an axis (X-X), and a coaxial core (220), rotatably mounted around the axis. An upstream part (220.1) of the core extends into the casing so that a material flow channel (230) is delimited between them, with an annular cross-section and centred on the axis. A downstream part (220.2) of the core extends outside the casing and is coupled to a rotation drive motor (250). A male divergent (260) is fixedly secured to the casing and received coaxially in the casing so that a passage (270) is delimited between them, connecting a central inlet (211) of the casing and an upstream end (230A) of the channel. The passage is shaped so that the material progresses therein, forming a flow (6) which diverges from the axis towards the downstream and is distributed around the axis. The male divergent is axially abutted to the upstream part of the core, supporting it and guiding it in rotation. Figure for the abstract: 2.

title: Method of processing
abstract: A method for processing a plant product comprises processing the plant product to create a pomace portion and a juice portion and then further processing at least one of the pomace portion and the juice portion. Further processing of the juice portion comprises heating, adding flocculant and cooling. Preferably any solids present are separated from the juice portion to produce a liquid portion and a solids portion, e.g. by centrifugation, pressing or sieving. Further processing of the pomace portion comprises fermenting. The method preferably does not include the addition of an acid. The plant product may be a Brassicaea, Apiaceae and/or Cannabaceae, e.g. broccoli, cauliflower, carrot, parsley, coriander and/or industrial hemp. The plant product may comprise a side stream product. Creating the juice and pomace portions may be achieved by pressing or maceration. The flocculant is preferably selected from sagina subulata, Chondrus crispus, polyglutamic acid, succinoglycan, sclerotium gum, chitosan, cellulose-based flocculants, starch-based flocculants and/or lignin. The pomace portion may be fermented by mixing in a culture comprising a bacteria selected from the genera bifidobacterium, staphylococcus, debaryomyces, penicillium, leuconostoc, lactobacillius, pediococcus and/or streptococcus.

Furthermore, the invention relates to novel methods for enhancing the expression and/or translation of RNA, i.e. protein expression, and to methods for improving the stability of an RNA molecule. The invention also involves reducing the activation of innate sensing, interferon generation and/or degradation of an RNA molecule in a host. The invention also incorporates the use of the RNA molecules in vaccines and other therapeutic pharmaceutical compositions, and their use in immunisation and therapy, such as RNAi, gene therapy, gene editing and protein replacement. In particular, the invention relates to locked nucleotides and locked nucleic acid (LNA)-RNA molecules, and the use or incorporation of such locked nucleotides and LNA-RNA molecules in any of the above applications.

title: Foodstuff
abstract: A vegan yoghurt comprises a filamentous fungus and mesophilic bacteria and/or its residue. Preferably, the bacteria is live lactic-acid producing bacteria, e.g., mesophilic Lactococci or Lactobacilli, i.e., Lactococcus lactis subsp. lactis. Preferably, the yogurt includes thermophilic bacteria, preferably, lactic-acid producing bacteria, i.e., Streptococcus thermophilus, Pediococcus acidilacti, Lactobacillus delbrueckii spp bulgaricus; Lactobacillus acidophilus; Lactobacillus helveticus; and Bifidobacteria sp. Preferably, the yoghurt includes at least 106 CFUs of mesophilic bacteria and the fungus has filaments <50μm and/or comprises fungal mycelia. Preferably, the fungus is Fusarium venenatum A3/5. Preferably, the yogurt includes 5-10wt% filamentous fungus and 4-14wt% plant-based milk, preferably, coconut milk. Preferably, the yogurt has a protein content of 3-25g/100g. Also claimed is a process for making the yogurt, which may comprise inoculating the filamentous fungus and a plant milk with mesophilic bacteria culture at 37°C or more. Preferably, the fermentation process takes place at 38°C or less and may produce a mixture with pH 4.5 or lower. The use of such a mesophilic bacteria starter culture results in a reduction in off taste of the yoghurt.

title: A METHOD OF PRODUCING SINGLE CELL PROTEIN FROM WHEY
abstract: The present invention is generally concerned with the field of microbial fermentation of dairy or dairy alterative industry waste material and microbial protein production such as single cell protein (SCP). In particular the present invention is directed to microbial fermentation of dairy derived or dairy alternative derived whey for production of single cell proteins (SCP) or microbial biomass. More in particular, the present invention relates to a method of producing a single cell protein or biomass, comprising propagating a microbial culture in a large scale setting under suitable conditions and growth medium comprising dairy-derived whey to produce a single cell protein, where the microbial culture comprises microalgae, yeast and bacterial species (Figure 1). The present invention also relates to method of identifying a strain of microorganism, or mixture of strains of microorganisms, capable of efficiently using dairy-derived whey waste as a food source to produce biomass as a source of single cell protein. The present invention also relates to a propagated microbial culture or a composition and use of the culture in microbial fermentation. The present invention further provides a product or supplement comprising the composition of the present invention.

title: A method of producing single cell protein from whey
abstract: A method of producing single cell protein SCP or biomass comprises culturing microbial inoculum in a growth medium comprising dairy-derived whey. The method may comprise (i) inoculating growth medium comprising dairy-derived whey with a microbial inoculum to form an inoculated microbial mixture, (ii) incubating the inoculated microbial mixture at a first incubation temperature to generate a propagated starter culture, (iii) adding the starter culture to a growth medium comprising dairy-derived whey to form a fermentation mixture and incubating the fermentation mixture, and (iv) treating the fermentation mixture to produce a SCP. The fermentation mixture may be incubated at a second incubation temperature for at least 24 hrs. At least one of the strains in the microbial inoculum may be a microalga, a yeast, a fungi or a bacteria. The propagated starter culture preferably comprises a mixture of at least two strains of microalgae, at least two strains of fungi, at least two strains of yeast, and at least two strains of bacteria. A product or supplement comprising the biomass, a propagated microbial culture and use of the culture in microbial fermentation, and a method of identifying microorganisms capable of efficiently producing biomass using dairy-derived whey are also claimed.

abstract: The present invention relates to plant-based protein ingredients suitable for use in consumables, including vegetarian or vegan meat and dairy analogues. These plant-based protein ingredients possess desirable organoleptic properties resulting from improved plant genetics methodologies. Claim 1: A method for modifying a gelation pattern of the pea protein ingredient from a Pisum sativum plant, the method comprising the following steps: (i) providing at least one pea comprising at least one nucleic acid molecule comprising at least one modification of a nucleotide sequence of at least one gene, including its regulatory region, wherein the at least one modified gene encodes a convicillin protein, wherein said at least one modification affects the gelation pattern of the pea protein ingredient, wherein said at least one modification affects at least one nucleotide sequence of a reference gene Psat06G0558100 (SEQ ID No. 2) compared to the variant of the reference gene Psat06G0558100 (SEQ ID No. 1) and/or of a reference gene Psat06G0558200 (SEQ ID No. 66) compared to the variant of the reference gene Psat06G0558200 (SEQ ID No. 65), or a combination thereof; (ii) optionally: cultivating the Pisum sativum plant to obtain at least one pea comprising a protein composition having a modified gelation pattern compared to a Pisum sativum plant not comprising the at least one modified convicillin gene, or the regulatory region thereof; and (iii) obtaining a pea protein ingredient from said Pisum sativum plant, wherein said pea protein ingredient obtained, preferably as an intermediate, has a modified gelation pattern, wherein the modified gelation pattern is defined as a modified ratio of vicilin to convicilin in a pea protein ingredient, preferably in a pea flour, compared to the reference ratio of vicilin to convicilin of 2:1 to 4:1 (w/w) of a pea protein ingredient, preferably a flour, from a reference Pisum sativum plant, wherein the modified ratio of vicilin to convicilin is characterized by a reduced amount of convicilin compared to the amount measured for the reference Pisum sativum plant and, therefore, an increased ratio of vicilin to convicilin.

title: COMPOSITIONS AND METHODS FOR DIAGNOSING AND/OR TREATING CHRONIC KIDNEY DISEASE
abstract: Compositions and methods diagnose and/or treat chronic kidney disease (CKD) using one or more feline circulating proteins as markers for early-stage CKD. A method of diagnosing chronic kidney disease (CKD) in a feline can include measuring an amount of each of at least one circulating protein from the feline. The at least one circulating protein is one or more of adiponectin (ADIPOQ), cathelicidin (CAMP), kinesin-like protein (KIF12), plasma retinol-binding protein (RBP4), Ig-like domain-containing protein (ZKSCAN1), coagulation factor X (F10), fibronectin (FN1) and mixtures thereof. title: PLANT-BASED MICROFIBROUS SCAFFOLDS FOR CULTURING MEAT
abstract: The present disclosure relates to plant-based microfibrous scaffolds and a method for producing these scaffolds for culturing meat, providing a biocompatible, edible, and scalable 3D structure that supports high cell yield. The scaffold comprises plant-based proteins, polysaccharides, and carbohydrates, eliminating the need for synthetic polymers and toxic solvents. The method for producing these scaffolds comprises dissolving the components, creating a homogeneous solution, spinning the fibers using air volume and centrifugal forces, and heating to achieve crosslinking. The resulting scaffolds have controlled fiber diameters, thicknesses, and area densities, enhancing cell growth, nutrient diffusion, and structural integrity and provide an efficient and sustainable solution for large-scale cultured meat production.

abstract: The subject of the application is a plant drink containing water, a source of protein and fat, including peas and a stabilizer, which is characterized in that it is a mixture of 90% by weight of water and 10% by weight of powdered peas, beans, sunflower seeds, sunflower oil and a polysaccharide stabilizer, in which the carbohydrate content is 2.9 to 3.38 g/100 ml, the protein content is 2.05 to 2.32 g/100 ml, the fat content is from 3.12 to 3.35 g/100 ml and is obtained by the method specified below. title: Method of improving the maturity of low-quality marinated herring meat using digestive proteases
abstract: The subject of the application is a method for improving the meat maturity of marinated herring of low technological quality (caught during the feeding season) using digestive proteases, which is characterized in that prior to marinating, fresh or frozen-thawed herring fillets of low technological quality are stored for 4 to 5 days in a raw digestive protease preparation (SPPT) and/or injected with a raw digestive protease preparation (SPPT). Storage is carried out under refrigerated conditions (preferably at a temperature of 0°C -2°C) for 1 to 24 hours (preferably no more than 4 - 8 hours), in a herring fillet to raw digestive protease preparation (SPPT) ratio of 2:1 to 1:2 (weight:weight). During injection, from 0.1% to 10% of the raw digestive protease preparation (SPPT) is used relative to the weight of the herring fillets. For storage and/or injection, a crude preparation of digestive proteases (SPPT) is used, obtained as described in Polish patent application No. P.443190. The SPPT production method involves mixing ground fish digestive tract with a 1%-10% aqueous ethanol solution in a 1:1-10 (weight:volume) ratio, homogenizing the mixture, and then separating the precipitate. Before adding the aqueous ethanol solution or after separating the precipitate after homogenization, NaCl is added to achieve a final concentration of at least 3%, mixing, and then separating the precipitate to obtain a crude preparation of digestive proteases from fish after both steps.

title: Method for producing, in particular, milk foam, and a device for carrying out the method
abstract: In a method for producing, in particular, milk foam in a container (12) containing the milk, hot steam is supplied at a controllable rate and with air through a steam device immersed in the milk (13) in the container (12). The milk temperature is measured and evaluated during heating by at least one temperature probe (18) within the container (12). When heating of the milk (13) filled in the container (12) begins, steam is supplied at a predetermined rate, and the air supply is switched on. After the steam supply has started, a temperature difference between the measured milk temperatures at a predetermined first and a second fixed time is determined. Based on the temperature difference, at least the hot steam is supplied either at the same or at a modified rate and is switched off before or when the final temperature of the milk (13) is reached.

When the stage of heating up the milk (13) contained in the receptacle (12) begins, steam is supplied with a predetermined quantitative output, and the supply of air is switched on. title: Fermented protein extract from milk thistle - Sylibum marianum and method of obtaining it
abstract: The subject of the invention is a fermented protein extract from milk thistle - Sylibum marianum for use in the food industry. Fermented protein extract from milk thistle - Sylibum marianum contains from 3.87 to 8.19 g dry matter/100 mL of extract; from 0.77 to 2.3 g protein/100 mL of extract; from 0.63 to 1.12 g digestible carbohydrates/100 mL of extract; from 0.65 to 0.89 g total sugars/100 ml of extract; from 1.19 to 3.32 g total fat/100 mL of extract and from 0.03% to 0.06% salt. The application also includes a method for obtaining a fermented protein extract from milk thistle - Sylibum marianum, which is characterized in that the raw material in the form of milk thistle is ground at a rotational speed of not less than 4400 rpm for 30 - 40 s, then water at a temperature of 4°C - 20°C is added to the ground raw material while maintaining the mass fraction of the raw material to water between 1:5 and 1:15, the whole is mixed intensively for 15 - 20 s at a rotational speed of min. 4400 rpm, in the next stage, anhydrous sodium carbonate is added to the mixture of water and crushed raw material in such an amount that the pH of the extraction mixture is in the range of 7.8 - 8.2 at a temperature of 37°C - 40°C and the milk thistle protein extraction process is carried out, after which the mixture is centrifuged at 3500 - 4500 rpm for 5 - 10 min, beet syrup is added to the centrifuged milk thistle (supernatant) in the amount of 20 - 30 g of syrup/1 L of centrifuged extract, and then the milk is pasteurized or sterilized, in the final stage, freeze-dried strains of lactic acid bacteria (LAB) and/or probiotic bacteria are added in the amount of 0.1 g of lyophilisate/1 L of milk, and then the incubation is carried out at the optimal temperature for the growth of the lactic acid bacteria used in the process lactic acid, wherein the fermentation process is carried out until the pH of the fermented milk thistle is in the range of 4.50 - 4.70, obtaining the final product in the form of a fermented protein extract from milk thistle - Sylibum marianum.

title: Method of producing a fermented plant drink based on walnut and fermented plant drink based on walnut
abstract: The subject of the application is a method for producing a fermented plant drink based on walnuts and a fermented plant drink based on walnuts. In the method for producing a fermented plant drink containing a filtered water extract produced from a suspension containing water, walnuts, dried dates and flax seeds, fermented by yogurt bacteria, the suspension is formed from a mixture of separately washed, shelled (10), crushed walnuts (11) in an amount of 83.2% to 83.9% by weight in the mixture, crushed dried dates (13) in an amount of 0.0% to 12.6% by weight in the mixture, and crushed flax seeds (12) in an amount of 3.8% to 5.0% by weight in the mixture, with a grain size after crushing of 0.05 mm to 0.1 mm and water in an amount of 74.0% to 77.0% by weight in the suspension, which is poured over the mixture, and the resulting suspension is mixed (14) and is subjected to extraction (15), with continuous stirring, at a rotational speed of 1900 to 2100 rpm at a temperature of 28°C to 32°C for 14 to 16 minutes, and the resulting extract is filtered, poured into individual packages and pasteurized in individual packages, and then cooled to a temperature of 38°C to 42°C and inoculated with a mixture of bacterial strains of Streptococcus thermopilus, Lactobacillus delbrueckii ssp. bulgaricus, Lactobacillus acidophilus and Bifidobacterium lactis. and incubated at the above temperature.

abstract: The present invention is directed to bioelectronic systems for monitoring, optimising, developing and/or controlling biological systems, especially cultivated meat products and methods for producing cultivated meat products. The measurement of electric current(s) passing through cells, tissues and/or areas surrounding the cells or tissues, including media, is used to estimate the number of cells and thus cell growth over time and can also be used to estimate the differentiation of cells which is the change of phenotype of cells, along with media composition, the presence of contaminants, viable cell density, and other characteristics of the cells, tissue and/or media that has been measured. Artificial intelligence, including machine learning algorithms may be used to analyze and process the data that has been measured. Additionally, an electrical stimulus can be used to promote cell growth, function, and/or differentiation.

title: METHODS OF PREPARATION OF FOOD COMPOSITIONS AND BEVERAGES BASED ON WHOLE ALMOND, PECAN OR WALNUT FRUITS AND RELATED PRODUCTS
abstract: Described is a method of processing nut fruits selected from almond fruits, pecan fruits and/or walnut fruits, comprising: a) off-ground harvesting of the nut fruits; b) subjecting a mass comprising kernels, inner shell and green outer hull of the nut fruits to grinding to an average particle size of 500 μm or less to provide a ground mass; and c) further processing the ground mass to edible nut fruit solids, edible nut fruit-based products and/or nut fruit beverages; wherein the nut fruits have not been subjected to drying before step b). The method provides an ecologically friendly and simple alternative for processing almond fruits, pecan fruits and/or walnut fruits to food and beverage compositions that are not only suitable for human consumption but simultaneously comprise high amounts of the natural antioxidants and bioactive materials present in the fresh fruits. Simultaneously, the method reduces risks related to both consumer health and the orchard environment, does not require extensive use of herbicides and/or pesticides, and reduces dust generation and tree water stress. In addition, edible products and beverages obtained by the aforementioned method are described.

title: CELL CULTURE CONSTRUCT
abstract: A food product cell culture construct for a food product bioreactor module (102) that is attachable to a food product cell culturing system (100). The food product cell culture bioreactor module (102) has a housing (108) adapted to receive the food product cell culture construct for culturing cells on the food product cell culture construct within the housing. The food product cell culture construct comprises a plurality of fibres (120) and an end support (126). The plurality of fibres (120) have external surfaces for cell adhesion and culturing, and ends embedded within the end support (126) and extending from the end support (126) such they extend into the housing (108) when the food product cell culture construct is received in the housing of the food product cell culture bioreactor module (102). At a plane coincident with the end support (126) the plurality of fibres (120) are arranged in a fibre distribution defining an envelope. The fibre distribution comprises a Fibre Distribution Parameter, FDP, of between 9 cm3 and 24 cm3, the FDP being the product of the sum of the circumferences of the plurality of fibres within the envelope and the area within the envelope not occupied by the plurality of fibres.

abstract: The present invention relates to a fish cutting apparatus and a method for cutting fish fillets from the bones of the fish, wherein the fish cutting apparatus may reduce the initial costs and maintenance costs, but still be easy to operate and provide a substantially satisfactory filleting result. title: SYSTEMS AND METHODS FOR RAPID LIQUID BIOPRINTING
abstract: Methods for fabricating three-dimensional (3D) constructs from a mixture of cells, culture medium, and a scaffold material with a controlled calcium chloride concentration is disclosed. The process involves positioning a nozzle within a gel composed of alginate solution. The nozzle is then moved within the gel, releasing the cell-media-scaffold mixture in a controlled pattern. As the mixture is deposited, it becomes surrounded by the gel, which provides structural support until it solidifies through the cross-linking reaction between the calcium chloride in the cell-media-scaffold mixture and the alginate solution. This results in the formation of a solid 3D structure that incorporates the cells and their supporting scaffold. The presented method offers a versatile platform for generating intricate cell-based 3D constructs with precise control over their composition and structure. This method can be used to produce cultivated meat with complex 3D structures as well as organelles and fully functional organs.

title: Frozen extruded plant-based meat substitutes and method of producing frozen extruded plant-based meat substitutes
abstract: The invention relates to frozen extruded plant-based meat substitutes produced without soy, containing whole-grain flours, especially from the seeds of domestic high-protein legumes and/or oil plants as single flours and/or in mixtures in various proportions, allowing to obtain meat substitutes with a high protein content, fiber and high firmness. Frozen, plant-based, extruded soy-free meat substitutes obtained by extruding a composition of ingredients containing pea protein isolate or wheat protein isolate, high-protein legume flour and/or oilseed flour, as individual flours or in mixtures, with or without additives, are characterized in that they contain legume flour and/or oilseed flour in a total amount of not less than 30% of the amount of bulk components relative to the weight of bulk components, wherein the number of individual ingredients in the mixtures is arbitrary, and furthermore they contain pea protein isolate and/or wheat protein isolate in an amount from 10% to 70% of the weight of bulk components. Preferably, the legume flour contains lupin flour, chickpea flour, red lentil flour, bean flour, and the oilseed flour contains flaxseed flour and sunflower flour. Preferably, they contain beetroot powder and/or paprika powder and/or tomato powder and/or turmeric powder and/or inactive yeast powder and/or grape seed extract powder. The method for producing frozen, plant-based extruded meat substitutes according to the invention consists in extruding a mixture of ingredients containing pea protein isolate and/or wheat protein in an amount of 10% to 70% of the mass of bulk components, flour from high-protein legumes and/or oilseeds as individual flours or in mixtures in a total amount of not less than 30% of the amount of bulk components in relation to the mass of the raw materials of the final product, wherein the number of individual ingredients in the form of domestic flours in the mixtures is arbitrary, and the resulting products are frozen at a temperature of -30°C to -40°C. Preferably, lupin flour and/or chickpea flour and/or red lentil flour and/or bean flour is used as the legume seed flour, while flaxseed flour and/or sunflower flour is used as the oil seed flour. Preferably, the extrusion process is carried out with the addition of water greater than the share of dry ingredients. Preferably, native starches are added to the mixture during mixing in an amount of 0.1% to 5.0% of the bulk components relative to the total weight of the raw materials. Furthermore, beetroot powder and/or paprika powder and/or tomato powder and/or turmeric powder and/or powdered inactive yeast and/or powdered grape seed extract are preferably added as coloring additives or mixtures thereof.

title: Dried extruded plant meat substitutes and method of producing dried extruded plant meat substitutes
abstract: The aim of the invention is to provide dried, extruded, soy-free plant-based meat substitutes containing whole-grain flours from seeds, particularly domestic high-protein and/or legume plants, as single flours and/or in blends in any proportions, enabling meat substitutes with high protein and fiber content and high water absorption. The aim is also to develop a method for their production. The invention concerns dried, extruded, soy-free plant-based meat substitutes obtained by extruding a composition of ingredients containing pea protein isolate, flour from high-protein legumes and/or oilseeds as individual ingredients or in blends, and optionally the addition of natural colorants. These substitutes contain flour from high-protein legumes and/or oilseeds as individual ingredients or in blends in an amount of no less than 30% of the total weight of the raw materials. Preferably, dried, extruded plant-based meat substitutes contain lupin flour, chickpea flour, red lentil flour, and bean flour as legume seed flour, while the oilseed flour contains flaxseed flour, hemp flour, and sunflower flour, and as coloring ingredients, they contain beetroot powder and/or paprika powder and/or tomato powder and/or turmeric powder and/or powdered inactive yeast. Preferably, they contain rosemary extract as an oxidizing additive. The invention also relates to a method for producing dried extruded plant meat substitutes, which consists in mixing a protein isolate with legume seed flour and/or oil seed flour with the addition of water, wherein a single ingredient or a mixture of ingredients is present in an amount of not less than 30% of the amount of bulk components in relation to the total weight of the raw materials, is subjected to extrusion and then shaped in a forming die to a specific shape and cut to the desired size and dried, wherein the legume seed flour preferably comprises lupin flour, chickpea flour, red lentil flour, bean flour, and the oil seed flour comprises linseed flour, hemp flour, and sunflower flour. Preferably, beetroot powder and/or paprika powder and/or tomato powder and/or turmeric powder and/or inactive yeast powder are used as coloring ingredients, and rosemary extract is used as an oxidizing additive.

title: INSECT OIL AS A SOURCE OF FAT IN MILK REPLACEMENTS FOR YOUNG RUMINANTS
abstract: INSECT OIL AS A FAT SOURCE IN MILK REPLACEMENTS FOR YOUNG RUMINANTS. The present invention relates to a sustainable fat source that can replace coconut oil, which has disadvantages from a sustainability perspective, as an additive in milk replacers for young ruminants. Milk replacers for young ruminants must provide not only high-quality proteins but also energy for maintenance and growth. A substantial portion of the energy in milk replacers comes primarily from fat. This fat typically comes from coconut oil, a significant portion (between 18% and 40%). Until now, reliance on coconut oil has been high, making the system vulnerable to disruptions. The sustainable solution according to the present invention involves the use of insect oil.

title: ALTERNATIVE FOR PALM OIL REPLACEMENT AS A SOURCE OF FAT IN MILK REPLACEMENTS FOR YOUNG RUMINANTS
abstract: ALTERNATIVE FOR PALM OIL REPLACEMENT AS A FAT SOURCE IN MILK REPLACEMENTS FOR YOUNG RUMINANTS. Milk replacers for young ruminants must provide not only high-quality proteins but also energy for maintenance and growth. The energy in milk replacers comes largely from fat. This fat is primarily derived from the oil palm. Palm oil is a readily available raw material with an attractive price. Furthermore, it has good digestibility and a suitable fatty acid profile similar to animal fat, with a relatively high proportion of C16:0 as a saturated long-chain fatty acid. The dependence on palm oil is high, making the system vulnerable to disruptions. The alternative product according to the present invention eliminates this vulnerability while also being highly digestible and having a suitable fatty acid profile.

title: FUNCTIONAL EXTRACTION OF PROTEIN
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a method for producing functional proteins, and in particular, functional soy protein concentrate (FSPC). This method bypasses the multi-step processes of conventional techniques by integrating the functionalization step directly into the alcohol extraction process. The process involves treating a protein source, such as soy white flakes or soy protein concentrate powder, with an alcohol solution comprising alcohol, an alkali hydroxide, and a reducing agent. This treatment process eliminates the need for separate hydration, pH adjustment, high-temperature short-time (HTST) treatment, and separate drying steps, notably removing spray drying in general. This disclosure also encompasses the functional soy protein produced by the disclosed method and its use in various food applications.

title: Pulse seed-based non-dairy composition and associated methods
abstract: Methods of removing plant tone of starchy Fabaceae pulses are disclosed. The pulses are selected from chickpea (Cicer arietinum), yellow pea (Pisum sativum), common bean (Phaseolus vulgaris) and fava bean (Vicia faba), and can be hulled or de-hulled pulses, whole pulses, split pulses or chopped solids having a Feret diameter of 1 to 4 mm. The pulses are transformed in an emulsifying and emulsion stabilizing manner suitable for fermentation. The emulsion thereof may be used in fermented milk derivatives that have a desirable texture or form that melts or self-disintegrates in-mouth. To achieve these technical effects, the pulses are pretreated with an aqueous bicarbonate (MHCO3) solution or bicarbonate/carbonate (M2CO3) solution of bicarbonate salt, bicarbonate salt and carbonate salt, or bicarbonate salt and hydroxide salt (MOH), wherein M is an alkali metal cation, and having a pH between pH 7 and 10, preferably between 7.5 and 10.

abstract: A method of operating a bioreactor for growing meat and a corresponding bioreactor. title: Device, method and use of a device for separating a starting material
abstract: Shown and claimed is a device for separating a starting material into components of different flowability by means of a perforated drum and a rotating functional belt. The functional belt is guided over a plurality of rollers, of which a tension roller keeps the functional belt taut and a pressure roller presses the functional belt against the perforated drum with an adjustable force. The device comprises a lever arrangement and a pressure pneumatic cylinder. By pivoting the lever arrangement using the pressure pneumatic cylinder, the position of the pressure roller can be changed and thus the force with which the functional belt presses against the perforated drum can be adjusted. Furthermore, a method for separating a starting material into components of different flowability and the use of a device for separating a starting material into components of different flowability are shown and claimed.

title: Chicken egg substitute that does not contain any animal-derived ingredients
abstract: The subject of the invention is a chicken egg substitute that does not contain ingredients of animal origin (suitable for people on a vegan diet) for use in food products. The purpose of the invention is to present the composition and proportions of a dry composition of ingredients intended for mixing (mixing) with water, allowing for obtaining constant organoleptic properties and reproducing most of the physical and chemical properties of a chicken egg. The egg replacer containing no animal-derived ingredients is in the form of a dry powder consisting of hydrophilic polymers in the form of polysaccharides or polysaccharide-derived substances (from 6% to 10% by weight of the dry composition), vegetable protein (from 8% to 15% by weight of the dry composition), inactive yeast (4% by weight of the dry composition), guar gum (3.5% by weight of the dry composition), tapioca starch (from 70% to 78.5% by weight of the dry composition), and in another version of the invention carrageenan (from 3% to 5% by weight of the dry composition), vegetable protein (from 8% to 15% by weight of the dry composition), inactive yeast (4% by weight of the dry composition), guar gum (3.5% by weight of the dry composition), tapioca starch (from 72.5% to 80% by weight of the dry composition), and before use It is mixed with water in a ratio of 10% powder to 90% water.

title: DEVICE, METHOD AND SYSTEM FOR DETECTING THE BEHAVIOUR OF FISH IN ORDER TO IMPROVE THE FEEDING PROCESS THEREOF
abstract: The present invention proposes a device, method and system for detecting the behaviour of a group of fish in order to improve the feeding process thereof, based on passive acoustics of hydrodynamic noise produced by the school of fish and the use of artificial intelligence. Specifically, a method, device and smart system is proposed, which, by means of at least one acoustic sensor, collects the acoustic signal generated by the movement of the fish during feeding, processes the signal and implements models developed using artificial intelligence in order to determine the feeding status of the fish. By means of these models, the efficiency of the feeding process of the population being farmed is detected, enabling, among other advantages real-time decision-making in order to manage the feeding process and reduce the amount of wasted food, thereby optimising feed conversion rates.

abstract: The disclosure relates to a slicing machine for slicing foods, comprising: a feed unit adapted to feed at least one product caliber in a feed direction, a cutting unit, and a control unit adapted to control at least the feed unit and the cutting unit. The control unit is adapted to be in signal connection with a processing apparatus separate from the slicing machine. The processing apparatus is adapted to process the product caliber before it is sliced by the slicing machine. The control unit is further adapted to receive at least one dimension and/or a weight and/or a density of the at least one product caliber or data representative thereof from the processing apparatus and to control the feed unit and/or the cutting unit based on the at least one dimension and/or the weight and/or the density. abstract: A freshness detection method of an object and a refrigeration appliance comprise the steps of collecting gas data in a cavity, inputting the gas data into a preset model group to obtain a candidate result group, wherein the preset model group comprises a plurality of preset models, the candidate result group comprises a plurality of candidate prediction results, the preset models are used for predicting the freshness of the object according to the input gas data, training sets for training different preset models are at least partially derived from different experimental batches, the training sets comprise gas data of the object with single dimension under a plurality of freshness, and a voting method is adopted to obtain the freshness detection result based on the candidate result group. title: Beverage makers and their use
abstract: A beverage maker is provided, comprising a frothing unit for frothing milk, a milk line connected to the frothing unit and featuring a mixing chamber, a control unit, a mixing line, and an input unit. The mixing line connects the milk line to a source of the beverage maker containing a liquid with a lower fat content and/or a lower carbon footprint than milk, and the mixing line includes a valve. The beverage maker's control unit is configured to control or regulate the mixing line's valve based on a signal received from the beverage maker's input unit. This allows a user of the beverage maker to select a beverage from a variety of different options based on its cost, lightness (in terms of fat content), and carbon footprint.

title: METHOD AND SYSTEM FOR TREATING STEAM CONDENSATE OBTAINED BY HIGH-PRESSURE GENERATOR FOR OBTAINING CARBON DIOXIDE ABSORPTION SOLUTION
abstract:
FIELD: chemistry.
SUBSTANCE: invention relates to a method for treating steam condensate generated in a high-pressure regenerator operating at a pressure in the range from 1.0 to 1.2 kg/cm2, for regenerating a carbon dioxide absorption solution. The method comprises capturing carbon dioxide in a carbon dioxide absorption plant using a carbon dioxide absorption solution and feeding the obtained carbon dioxide absorption solution containing absorbed carbon dioxide into a high-pressure regenerator of a heat exchange system comprising a high-pressure regenerator containing a regenerated solution and a steam reboiler. The method also comprises feeding low-pressure steam with a pressure in the range from 3.2 to 3.5 kg/ cm2 into the steam reboiler to supply heat to the high-pressure regenerator. In the steam reboiler, due to heat exchange of the steam with the carbon dioxide absorption solution containing absorbed carbon dioxide, the carbon dioxide absorption solution containing absorbed carbon dioxide is heated, resulting in steam condensate and a regenerated carbon dioxide absorption solution. The regenerated carbon dioxide absorption solution exiting the high-pressure regenerator is subjected to further treatment in a low-pressure regenerator operating at a pressure below 0.2 kg/cm2. The method further comprises a step of directly feeding the steam condensate obtained in the steam reboiler into a deaerator to obtain an aqueous solution suitable for producing steam with an oxygen content below 20 parts per billion. The present invention also relates to a system for performing this method, to the use of the system and to a method for modernising the system.
EFFECT: use of the full heat content of the steam condensate generated by the high-pressure regenerator, while ensuring that the equipment in the plant is not subjected to corrosion.

title: FOAMING INGREDIENT
abstract:
FIELD: food industry.
SUBSTANCE: disclosed is a porous soluble foaming ingredient. Ingredient has closed porosity from 20% to 80%, contains gas inclusions at pressure above atmospheric, wherein the ingredient contains from 60 to 97% of one or more carbohydrates in terms of dry substance and from 3% to 40% of vegetable protein in terms of dry substance. Vegetable protein is selected from the group consisting of pea protein, broad bean protein, gram protein, lentil protein, potato protein and combinations thereof, and the porous soluble foaming ingredient has a glass transition temperature of 50 °C to 90 °C, wherein the inclusions of gas are present in an amount sufficient to release at least 1 ml of gas at ambient conditions per gram of ingredient when adding aqueous liquid. Disclosed are: a soluble beverage powder containing a porous soluble foaming ingredient, a method of producing a porous soluble foaming ingredient comprising the following steps: a) spray drying a pressurized gas-saturated aqueous mixture containing vegetable protein and one or more carbohydrates to form a porous powder having a glass transition temperature, wherein aqueous mixture contains from 3 to 40% of vegetable protein in terms of dry substance, and the vegetable protein is subjected to homogenisation performed by means of a high pressure homogeniser; b) exposing the porous powder to a gas under pressure, wherein the porous powder is at a temperature above its glass transition temperature, such that closed pores present in the porous powder are filled with gas under pressure; c) cooling the porous powder to a temperature below its glass transition temperature; d) pressure release. Disclosed is use of porous soluble foaming ingredient for preparation of foaming beverage.
EFFECT: porous soluble foaming ingredient whose characteristics are close to those of milk-based ingredients, forms a greater volume of foam than casein milk protein; foam is more rigid and more stable.

title: METHOD OF PRODUCING PUMPED PASTE OF NUT OR STONE FRUIT SEEDS
abstract:
FIELD: food industry.
SUBSTANCE: invention relates to food industry. Method for preparation of pumped confectionary mass from seeds of stone fruits and/or nut fruits, in particular nuts, almonds or nut-almond mixtures, includes crushing of seeds of stone fruits or nut fruits, already extracted in the form of stones or peeled from shell, by means of preliminary crushing. Then the mass formed as a result of preliminary grinding is supplied to horizontal mixer (8). Then, in horizontal mixer (8), the mass formed as a result of preliminary grinding is subjected to the action of hot air with a temperature higher than 60 °C and below 100 °C and/or vacuum until rupture of walls of its cells remained intact after preliminary grinding. Process of exposure to hot air and/or vacuum is carried out until the residual moisture content is below 2.1%. After that, the mass formed as a result of preliminary grinding, as well as exposure to hot air and/or vacuum, respectively, is subjected to single-stage or multi-stage further grinding to obtain a pumped confectionary mass. Also disclosed is an apparatus for implementing said method. Plant comprises preliminary grinder (2), horizontal mixer (8), device (13) for supplying hot air or vacuum and a fine grinding device (11).
EFFECT: invention is aimed at production of pumpable nut paste without addition of ingredients other than stone fruit seeds or nut paste, and without change of taste of confectionary mass based on nut paste.

abstract: HEAT TREATED COMPOSITION, ITS USE AND ITS METHOD OF PREPARATION, FOOD PRODUCT AND ITS METHOD OF PREPARATION. The present invention relates to heat-treated compositions that include at least one vegetable protein source. The heat-treated composition may contain a reduced undesirable flavor and aroma from the at least one vegetable protein source and/or an increased desirable flavor and aroma that exhibits a distinct flavor and aroma note. Also disclosed are heat-treated food or beverage products containing the heat-treated composition, as well as methods of producing the heat-treated compositions and the heat-treated food or beverage products and methods of using the heat-treated compositions and the heat-treated food or beverage products.

title: PROCESS FOR OXIDATION OF BETA-CARYOPHYLENE
abstract: The present invention relates to a process for the oxidation of beta-caryophyllene with oxygen, in particular atmospheric oxygen, which dispenses with the use of catalysts, enzymes and solvents. Furthermore, the present invention provides a mixture comprising certain caryophyllene oxides and their use as a flavoring and/or odorant. The present invention also relates to products and semi-finished products comprising the mixture according to the present invention.
